 \section{Motivation and Problem Statement}\label{sec:motivation}
 
 Interpretability is moving from a tool for inspecting model decisions post hoc to a practical mechanism for improving and controlling models. As interpretations increasingly guide model correction, training, and inference~\parencite{Anders2020ClArC,Pahde2023R2R,Ross2017RightReasons,Komorowski2026AGD}, the question is not only whether predictions are accurate, but whether a model relies on evidence appropriate to its task and whether we can understand, question, and correct its use of that evidence.
-
-For example, attribution can help investigate whether a language model draws on supplied context or knowledge acquired during training~\parencite{Kahardipraja2025Atlas}. It can also guide responses toward the supplied instructions or evidence~\parencite{Komorowski2026AGD}.
+For example, attribution can help investigate whether a language model draws on supplied context or knowledge acquired during training~\parencite{Kahardipraja2025Atlas}. It can also guide decoding toward the supplied instructions or evidence~\parencite{Komorowski2026AGD}.
 
 For vision models, this question concerns a form of shared visual grounding. When we ask a machine what it sees, seek its help, or entrust it with a task, we expect some alignment between its use of visual information and our own understanding of the scene. A robot asked to grasp a cup should recognize its shape and position. A system assisting a radiologist should attend to signs of disease, rather than incidental clues about where the image was acquired---a shortcut documented in medical imaging~\parencite{Zech2018Pneumonia}. We therefore seek models whose decisions rest on task-relevant objects, features, and relations in a way we can understand and question. \textcite{Muttenthaler2025AligNet} show that human similarity judgments can guide visual representations toward closer agreement with human perception. Attribution offers a means of investigating this alignment, providing evidence for communication, justified trust, and correction.
